sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed supplied nuisance fits. The observed experiment consists only of three mutually independent evaluation folds with projected law \(Q_P=P^n\otimes P^n\otimes P^n\). Every median-of-means statistic uses \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty near-equal consecutive blocks; the coverage and frontier claims apply for \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\).
sampling_model.units: Each fold contains \(n\) independent superpopulation observations \(Z_i=(X_i,T_i,Y_i)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment obeying \(T=g_0(X)+\eta\), with \(\eta\perp X\) and \(E_P[\eta^2]=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known unit treatment-residual variance is the nondegeneracy normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The statistical law class contains only primitive laws. The selected training-realized functions are external fixed inputs, and the upper theorem is uniform over all supplied pairs in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\). The Gaussian-coordinate converse is narrower: it applies to supplied-fit sequences for which the stated source fuzzy supports and a nonempty Gaussian two-point path transfer into the same projected class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The displayed rate in Theorem 3.2 contains nuisance-product and parametric terms, but its literal bounded-outcome class is incompatible with a nonzero partially linear slope under conditionally full-support Gaussian treatment noise and \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\). Appendix D equation (56) supplies the nuisance-product/log conclusion on the localized fuzzy supports, whereas equations (57)--(58) use an unbounded Gaussian-outcome witness for the separate parametric term. Theorem 5.4 gives a fixed-positive-cumulant ACE point-estimation upper bound on a separate class.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The conditionally transferred support-localized Gaussian product lower bound, the separately proved compatible parametric path, and Open-ended Questions 7--9

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 characterize expected-length adaptation over unions in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
The paper obtains composite-hypothesis lower bounds by moment-matched priors and chi-square control of normal mixtures.
Theorem 5 rules out second-order PLM orthogonality under Gaussian residuals, while Theorems 8--10 construct higher-order moments under non-Gaussian residuals.
Theorem 2 establishes coverage and interval-length control for the filtered union, while Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient.

body.tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). On supplied-fit sequences satisfying the stated conditional-transfer compatibility, the certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\): the nuisance-product/log term comes from the transferred support-localized JMS fuzzy construction, while \(n^{-1/2}\) comes from a separate compatible two-point family proved inside the present class. The literal full-class statement of JMS Theorem 3.2 is not used for this sum because its bounded-\(Y\), full-support Gaussian-treatment conditions force slope degeneracy under conditional outcome orthogonality, and its displayed root-\(N\) witness has unbounded Gaussian outcome. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is confined to the lower subexperiment. The within-non-Gaussian or constrained-risk branchwise converse and removal of the Gaussian logarithm remain open; no matching Pareto frontier or global union-supremum improvement is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Published structure-agnostic PLM theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length. The literal bounded-outcome formulation of JMS Theorem 3.2 also cannot be transferred wholesale to the present Gaussian branch: with conditionally full-support Gaussian treatment and \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\), bounded \(Y\) forces the partially linear slope to vanish, while its Appendix D root-\(N\) witness uses an unbounded Gaussian outcome.
project_justification.niche: The informative object is the two-coordinate expected-length region; the global union supremum remains governed by the Gaussian coordinate.
project_justification.fill: The proved upper component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion. The Gaussian converse is certified at \(d_n^-\) only under explicit conditional transfer of the source-localized nuisance-product supports and a compatible nonempty two-point path. The localized fuzzy construction supplies the product/log term, and the paper's own two-point argument supplies the parametric term; their maximum is converted to the displayed sum. The unsafe aggregate JMS lemma is removed rather than used as a full-class inclusion theorem. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is auxiliary to that lower subexperiment. The selector impossibility theorem closes the bounded-chi-square cross-branch fuzzy route at strong separation, while the actual strong-regime lower frontier remains open.

body.related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis inform two distinct pieces of the Gaussian-coordinate argument, but their literal full-class Theorem 3.2 is not used as a logical premise here. Its statement combines bounded \(Y\), conditionally full-support Gaussian treatment noise, and \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\); those conditions force a nonzero partially linear slope to be impossible because \(E[Y\mid X,T]=\theta T+f(X)\) would otherwise be unbounded in \(T\). Consistently with this mismatch, Appendix D equation (56) derives only the nuisance-product/log term at the retained \(\Lambda_n\) factor from moment-matched fuzzy supports, whereas equations (57)--(58) derive the parametric term using an unbounded Gaussian-outcome model. The present theorem conditionally transfers only the support-localized equation-(56) construction and independently proves the root-\(n\) term on a compatible embedded two-point path; it combines the two lower bounds through \(\max\{x,y\}\ge (x+y)/2\). Their Theorem 5.4 informs the fixed-separation ACE component but does not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. The auxiliary condition \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) is not attributed to their envelope and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length lower subexperiment. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned PLM residual. Cai and Low's 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier together with the conditional Gaussian coordinate just described; it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), not \(d_n\), and is conditional on two explicit compatibility requirements: transfer of the support-localized JMS fuzzy priors after outcome rescaling, and existence of a nonempty Gaussian two-point path around a compatible anchor. The cited localized fuzzy support supplies only the nuisance-product/log term; the parametric term is proved separately inside the paper and the two bounds are combined only afterward. The literal bounded-\(Y\) statement of JMS Theorem 3.2 cannot provide a direct full-class inclusion, because full-support Gaussian treatment plus conditional outcome orthogonality makes that bounded-outcome class slope-degenerate, and its Appendix D parametric witness instead has unbounded Gaussian outcome. The auxiliary subclass \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) is used only for this converse. The upper theorem needs none of these lower-experiment restrictions and does not identify a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early bounded-chi-square cross-branch Rademacher/Hermite route is resolved negatively at strong separation because the common-fit selector makes the mixtures asymptotically singular; a within-non-Gaussian or constrained-risk experiment is still required for the actual lower frontier.
body.honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All upper-frontier inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the upper theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The Gaussian lower theorem is explicitly conditional: for positive nuisance-product indices, only the source-localized fuzzy supports are invoked, with treatment radius \(\varepsilon_{g,n}/K\), outcome fit \(\widehat q/A\), and outcome radius \(\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\), followed by the pushforward \(S_A(x,t,y)=(x,t,Ay)\). A separate compatible two-point path supplies \(n^{-1/2}\). No direct inclusion of the literal JMS Theorem 3.2 class is asserted, because its bounded-outcome condition excludes the unbounded Gaussian-outcome root-\(N\) witness and is slope-degenerate under the present orthogonality condition. The novel restriction \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) defines only \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and is used only in that converse. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The branchwise converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.
